stem.text: The Grand Canyon is located in Arizona, USA. It is estimated to have formed over five million years ago as the Colorado River began to create a deep channel (canyon) in the surrounding rocks.
Before the canyon formed, an ancestral species of antelope squirrel lived in the area. An antelope squirrel is a type of rodent and member of the squirrel family, Sciuridae.
It is estimated that around 3.6 million years ago, an ancestral species diverged into the two species that are present today.

items: Harris’s antelope squirrel, Ammospermophilus harrisii, has its habitat range extending from

stem.text: the south rim of the canyon.

items: The white-tailed antelope squirrel, Ammospermophilus leucurus, has its habitat range

stem.text: extending from the north rim of the canyon.
Fig. 4.1 shows the location of the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon and the location of these species of antelope squirrel.
Suggest and explain how A. harrisii and A. leucurus evolved from an ancestral species.

points.text: 1 geographical, isolation / barrier (caused by the, river / canyon walls) ;
2 no gene flow between (isolated ancestral) populations ;
4 different / random / independent, mutations (in each population) ;
5 different changes in allele frequencies / different gene pools / different alleles selected for ;
6 populations have different, morphological / physiological / behavioral, features ;
7 leads to, reproductive isolation / inability to interbreed (to produce fertile offspring) ;

explanation.text: Isolation reduces gene flow. Mutation, selection and drift can then cause divergence until reproductive isolation remains even if populations come into contact again.

reasoningChain: Identify the barrier to gene flow.
Connect genetic divergence to the formation of reproductively isolated species.

inferredMistakes.text: Treating geographical separation alone as proof of completed speciation

stem.text: Scientists investigated the evolutionary relationships of the squirrel family, Sciuridae. The scientists took samples from the current species in the family and carried out DNA sequencing and morphological analysis.
To compare current species with species from the past:

items: specimens from museums were used to provide the tissue for DNA sequencing
teeth and skulls from fossils were compared as part of the morphological analysis.

stem.text: Describe the advantages of using DNA sequencing rather than morphological analysis to find out more about the evolutionary relationships of the squirrel family.

points.text: 1 provides more information (about the whole organism) ;
3 only a small sample of DNA is needed ;
4 can give estimate of when species diverged/how closely related two organisms are / molecular clock can estimate time of divergence ;
6 AVP ; e.g. idea of. avoids convergent evolution problems

explanation.text: Compare homologous DNA sequences at corresponding positions. Greater similarity generally supports a more recent common ancestor, but divergence-time estimates depend on assumptions about change rates.

reasoningChain: Separate evidence for relatedness from assumptions used to date divergence.

inferredMistakes.text: Treating a molecular divergence date as exact

stem.text: The estimate for the date that an ancestral species diverged into A. harrisii and A. leucurus is 3.58 million years ago. This estimate has a large uncertainty.
DNA sequencing, including DNA from fossils, was used to estimate this date of divergence.
Suggest a reason why there is such a large uncertainty for this date estimate.
